body:
IMO it's a good reason to upgrade our pinned Emscripten to a newer version. We could go with the current latest (6.0.5 at the time of writing) and pin that.

This requires thorough testing and review of the changelog as Emscripten often breaks our build (compile time issues) or JS features we rely on (runtime issues), so tests should include both compiling and running exported projects and the editor. Emscripten doesn't seem to follow semver so compat breakage can be found in any "patch" release.

> This is not reproducible if you compile against Emscripten 6.0.0.

Just as a heads-up, there may be another memory leak lurking alongside this one, so this statement might not be entirely true.

At some point I had added `use_assertions=no` to my build scripts and forgot about it. Now that I tried to build a build in the same way as the official builds does I omitted this argument, which means I'm back to `use_assertions=yes`, and for whatever reason this seems to cause similar memory leaks (100+ MiB) whenever you shut down the game, eventually prompting the browser to kill off the tab.

What's weird is that these `use_assertion=yes` memory leaks don't actually cause any leaks as far as Chrome's memory debugger is concerned, as the heap snapshots report a steady amount of memory, so I'm not sure what's going on exactly.

EDIT 1: This other leak might be a regression from #118771, but I have yet to figure out why exactly.
EDIT 2: Resolved as of #122056.
